meta.calc.title: Am I being paid right? NY home care pay check
meta.calc.description: Free calculator for New York home care aides, home health aides and CDPAP caregivers. Checks one week of pay against the {year} minimum wage, wage parity, overtime and 24-hour shift rules. Nothing you enter is saved.
meta.calc.appDescription: Free calculator that compares one week of a New York home care worker's pay with the state minimum wage, wage parity, overtime, 24-hour shift rules and PPL's posted CDPAP rate.
meta.ogAlt: CarePayNY: Am I being paid right? Free pay check and CDPAP guide for home care workers in New York.
footer.disclaimer.html: Estimates, not legal advice. CarePayNY explains New York's home care pay rules as of {date} and can't account for every situation. Union contracts (such as 1199SEIU), shift differentials, holiday pay, paid time off and other benefits can change what you're owed. The New York State Department of Labor enforces the state's wage laws.
footer.independent: We're independent and not affiliated with the New York State Department of Health, the Department of Labor, PPL or Medicaid. Rules version {version}.

meta.rates.description: New York home care pay rates for {y1} and {y2} in one table: home care aide minimum wage, general minimum wage, wage parity and PPL's CDPAP base pay, by region. With sources and a CSV download.
rates.h1: New York home care pay rates, {y1} and {y2}
rates.lead: In {y1}, the home care aide minimum wage in New York is {nyc1} an hour in New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, and {rest1} in the rest of the state. From {date2}, it is {nyc2} and {rest2}.
rates.note.html: These are minimum rates. Union contracts and agencies may pay more. The pay calculator checks one week of pay against these rules.
rates.caption: Hourly rates by year and region
rates.row.wpTotal: Wage parity: total pay and benefits
rates.pplCarried: PPL has not posted {year} rates yet. This is the latest rate PPL has posted.
rates.csv.html: Download this table as a CSV file (for spreadsheets). It has one line for each year, region and rate, with the date it took effect and its source. Rates that are not posted or do not apply are left out.
rates.def.hcaMin: Home care aide minimum wage: the lowest hourly pay New York law allows for home care aides. It covers agency aides, CDPAP personal assistants and workers hired directly by a family.
rates.def.generalMin: General minimum wage: the minimum for most other jobs. For home care, it applies only to work done now and then ("on a casual basis").
rates.def.wp: Wage parity: a state law for Medicaid-paid home care in New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester. The employer must give at least the total amount each hour, as pay, benefits or both. The benefit portion is the part above the minimum wage. Wage parity does not apply in the rest of the state.
rates.def.ppl: PPL's CDPAP base pay: the rate PPL says it pays CDPAP personal assistants. It depends on where the consumer (the person who gets care) lives.
calc.intro: For home care aides, home health aides and CDPAP caregivers in New York. Answer a few questions about one week of work and see what the law says you should be paid. Nothing you type is saved or sent anywhere.
calc.upcoming: New rates start {date}: the home care aide minimum goes up to {nyc} an hour in New York City, Long Island and Westchester, and {rest} in the rest of the state. This calculator uses them from that day.
calc.medicaid.q: Does Medicaid pay for your client's care?
calc.medicaid.hint: Most agency cases in NYC are Medicaid, often through a managed long-term care plan.

calc.shifts24: How many 24-hour shifts did you work this week?
calc.sleepMissed: Shifts where you did NOT get 8 hours for sleep, with 5 in a row
calc.mealsMissed: Shifts where you did NOT get 3 hours of meal breaks
calc.livesIn: I live in my client's home (it's where I sleep most nights)

row.wpTotal: Wage parity: total pay + benefits per hour
row.wpTotalMaybe: Wage parity: total pay + benefits per hour (if Medicaid)
row.wpGap: Benefits or extra cash owed on top of your rate

flag.privateFloor: If a family hires you directly, we use the home care aide minimum ({hca}). New York's law sets this minimum for any worker whose main job is helping a person at home with daily activities, such as bathing, dressing or eating. It doesn't cover someone who works only now and then ("on a casual basis"). For that kind of work, the general minimum wage ({general}) applies.
flag.shiftsMissed: On {count} of your 24-hour shifts you didn't get the required breaks, so you must be paid for more than 13 hours on those shifts (up to all 24). We counted {hours} paid hours for your 24-hour shifts.
flag.shiftsOk: 24-hour shifts can be paid as 13 hours only if you actually got 8 hours for sleep (5 of them uninterrupted) and 3 hours of meal breaks. If you were woken up or worked through meals, change the answers above.
flag.rateShort: Your hourly rate ({rate}) is below the minimum of {min} that applies to you by {short} an hour.
flag.pplShort: PPL says its base pay for CDPAP is {ppl} an hour when the person you care for lives in {region} (since {date}). The rate you entered is {short} less than that.
flag.stubShort: Your pay stub shows {entered}, about {diff} less than we'd expect for these hours.
flag.wageParity.yes: Because your work is Medicaid-funded in {region}, your employer must give you at least {total} an hour in total pay and benefits. With your rate, that's {gap} an hour in benefits (like health insurance or paid time off) or extra cash. The Wage Parity notice from your employer shows how they meet it.
flag.wageParity.maybe: Because your work may be Medicaid-funded in {region}, your employer must give you at least {total} an hour in total pay and benefits. With your rate, that's {gap} an hour in benefits (like health insurance or paid time off) or extra cash. The Wage Parity notice from your employer shows how they meet it.

summary.title: Home care pay check (NY rules {version})
calc.info.1: Home care workers have a right to a pay notice and a Wage Parity notice from their agency.
calc.info.2.html: CDPAP caregivers: PPL@Home, at pplfirst.com, shows each timesheet and its status. Our CDPAP guide explains PPL's payment messages.
calc.info.3.nyc.html: Free legal help in New York City: The Legal Aid Society helps low-wage workers with unpaid wages. More places: legal help by region.
calc.info.3.liw.html: The New York State Attorney General's Labor Bureau takes complaints about unpaid wages. Groups on Long Island and in Westchester: legal help by region.
calc.info.3.rest.html: Free legal help upstate: the Worker Justice Center of New York helps low-wage workers with unpaid wages. More places: legal help by region.
calc.info.4.html: The New York State Department of Labor takes wage claims. It's free to file a wage claim.
calc.rules.minimum: Home care aide minimum wage: {nyc}/hr in NYC, Long Island and Westchester; {rest}/hr elsewhere.
calc.rules.wageParity: Wage parity (Medicaid work): at least {nycTotal}/hr total in NYC ({nycBenefit} benefit) and {liwTotal}/hr in Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester ({liwBenefit} benefit).
calc.rules.shifts: 24-hour shifts: may be paid as 13 hours only with 8 hours for sleep (5 uninterrupted) and 3 hours for meals. Otherwise those hours must be paid.
calc.rules.overtime: Overtime: 1.5× your rate after 40 hours a week (44 if a family employs you directly and you live in their home).
calc.rules.note: Some state pages still show the older wage parity benefit of $4.09 (NYC) and $3.22 (Long Island and Westchester). The 2023 state budget lowered those to $2.54 and $1.67 from 2024 as the base wage rose, so total pay per hour went up. This tool uses the current amounts.

updates.title: Free email updates
updates.description: Get a short, free email when New York home care pay rules change, plus news about CDPAP and training.
updates.lead: Get a short email when New York home care pay rules change. We also send news about CDPAP and training. It is free and comes about once a month.

updates.what.3: News about training rules for home care aides
updates.lang: Each email is in English. At the top, it links to the same update on our website in Spanish, Chinese and Russian.
updates.form.consent.html: We will send one email to confirm. You get updates only after you click the link in it. Every update has a link to stop the emails. We don't share your address. Privacy Policy (in English).

updates.error.expired: That link has expired or doesn't work. You can sign up again below.

updates.check.title: Check your email

updates.confirm.title: Confirm your email updates
updates.confirm.body: Click the button to start getting free email updates from CarePayNY.
updates.confirm.nojs: To confirm, this page needs JavaScript turned on in your browser.
updates.done.title: You're signed up
updates.done.body: Thank you. You will get the next CarePayNY update by email. Every email has a link to stop the emails.
programs.title: Approved home care aide training programs in New York
programs.description: A list of the {n} home health aide (HHA) and personal care aide (PCA) training programs on the NYS Department of Health's approved list, by borough and county, with languages and phone numbers.
programs.jump: Jump to the list of programs ↓
programs.intro.html: This page lists the home care agencies and hospices whose aide training programs are approved by the New York State Department of Health. The list comes from the Department of Health's list dated {date}. It covers all of New York State: {n} places in {counties} counties, from New York City ({nyc}) to Long Island, the Hudson Valley, the Capital Region, Central and Western New York, the Southern Tier and the North Country.
programs.approval.html: Approval can change. The Department of Health updates its list from time to time. The Department of Health's list is the one that counts.
programs.labels.hha.html: HHA: a home health aide training program, at least 75 hours.
programs.labels.pca.html: PCA: a personal care aide training program, at least 40 hours.
programs.labels.hybrid.html: Part online: the Department of Health approved a hybrid program, which means part of the class is online and part is in person.
programs.labels.langs.html: Languages: next to each training, the languages it is approved to teach in. Each class is taught in one language.
programs.more.html: More about the two trainings, the skills test and the Home Care Registry: How to become a home care aide in New York. Program names and addresses below are in English, as the Department of Health lists them.
programs.cost.pca: A personal care aide program approved by the Department of Health may not charge any fee or tuition.
programs.cost.hha: A home health aide program approved by the Department of Health may charge up to $100, for things the trainee keeps.
programs.cost.free: Some agencies train people for free and plan to hire them after. Whether a program comes with a work agreement is something each program can explain.
programs.how.p: Programs are listed by region and county, then from A to Z. Being on this list is free. If a program ever pays for a featured spot, it will be labeled "Sponsored." CarePayNY is not part of the Department of Health, and a listing here is not a review or a promise of a job.
programs.tapHint: Tap a borough or county to see its programs.
programs.empty: No program on the list matches these choices. Fewer choices show more programs.
